newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC expects Vietnam refinery to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC expects Vietnam refinery to go ahead.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum said on Tuesday that PetroVietnam had rejected its bid for favourable terms under a multi-country consortium to build Vietnam's first refinery.

Chinese Petroleum, which said on Monday it was likely to pull out of the consortium, nevertheless said it expected the project to go ahead with foreign participation despite a newspaper report that PetroVietnam was terminating a joint venture formed to conduct a feasibility study for the project.
"Vietnam will go ahead to build the refinery," a senior Chinese Petroleum executive told Reuters in Taipei. "I believe LG Group and Stone & Webster will stay with the project."
South Korean industrial giant LG Group confirmed on Monday it was planning to stay with the project despite the expected pullout by Chinese Petroleum.

Tuesday's Asian Wall Street Journal reported that state-run PetroVietnam had sent a letter to its foreign suitors, including Chinese Petroleum, saying it was terminating a joint venture formed to undertake a feasibility study for the US$1.6 billion Dung Quat refinery.

The Chinese Petroleum executive described the fax as a "take it or leave it" proposition in which Vietnam rejected requests from Chinese Petroleum and other foreign partners that they be given preferential treatment.
"The fax reiterates PetroVietnam's position that terms for the project must be accepted as offered," he said.
Analysts have said the public wrangling between PetroVietnam and its foreign partners likely was a negotiating ploy by PetroVietnam to structure the investment to its best advantage.
By threatening to drop its foreign partners from the potentially lucrative project, PetroVietnam hoped to pressure its foreign partners to soften their terms, analysts said.
Chinese Petroleum said on Monday it was likely to leave the project after calculating it would be get at best only half of its expected 15 percent rate of return on its investment.
The Chinese Petroleum official said Malaysia's Petronas and U.S. refiner Conoco also were likely to withdraw their stakes in investment for the same reason.

If the three stay in, project equity would be split with Petrovietnam holding 30 percent, LG Group 27 percent, Petronas and Conoco 15 percent each, Chinese Petroleum and Chinese Investment Development Corp 10 percent and Stone & Webster three percent. Conoco is a unit of DuPont Co.
Chinese Petroleum's move was the latest in a string of setbacks for Vietnamese sponsor Petrovietnam, which denied as recently as February 13 that the consortium was wavering.
